metadata.name: ontological-self-criticism-example
metadata.notes: Reference fixture demonstrating provenance, distinction preservation, attack graphs, revision hooks, and retained dissent.

evidence.summary: Repeated examples showed that deliberate action was being forced into either conspiracy or accident, and descriptive language into either diagnosis or invalidity.
Abstract argumentation represents attacks among arguments and evaluates acceptability without requiring premature deletion of conflict.
PROV-O supplies interoperable concepts for entities, activities, agents, derivation, attribution, and generation.
Debate quality depends on diverse initial viewpoints and explicit calibrated confidence rather than homogeneous repetition alone.

claims.proposition: Deliberate institutional action does not entail secret centralized coordination.

potentialCollapses.risk: Intentional local decisions may be rejected unless evidence also proves a hidden central plan.
potentialCollapses.mitigation: Track intent evidence and coordination evidence as separate fields and permit distributed institutional intention.

potentialCollapses.risk: An emergent system result may be mislabeled accidental despite deliberate component actions.
potentialCollapses.mitigation: Represent intention at component and aggregate levels independently.

alternatives.proposition: Only centrally coordinated outcomes should be described as deliberate at the institutional level.
The outcome may be emergent while participating institutions still act deliberately.

defeaters.condition: Evidence shows the attributed institution had neither awareness nor control over the relevant local action.
The claim is used to imply coordination beyond the available evidence.

claims.proposition: A mature ontology ecology should detect when its own categories erase causally important middle spaces.

potentialCollapses.risk: Repeated agreement among correlated agents may be mistaken for independent support.
potentialCollapses.mitigation: Track source groups, first-pass independence, confidence, and dissent.

alternatives.proposition: Ontology stability is more important than retaining unresolved distinctions.

defeaters.condition: Self-revision repeatedly damages compatibility without measurable explanatory gain.

arguments.rationale: Intent can be demonstrated at the local institutional decision level without evidence of secret coordination.
Institution-level intent may be rhetorically overextended when decision authority is diffuse.
The claim is safe only when intent and coordination are recorded as distinct predicates.
Provenance, source diversity, and explicit counterpositions make ontology revision auditable rather than arbitrary.

decisions.rationale: Promote the distinction while retaining the objection as a live warning against over-attribution.
